meal.title: Choose the technology stack for the grocery app
meal.objective: Select Python Flask, MySQL, and Bootstrap based on team skills and project needs

voice.script: What’s the best combo to build a grocery app? You need a language for the back end, a database for data, and a UI framework for the look. First, ask your team: which languages do they already know? If most are comfortable with Python, Flask gives you a lightweight web server and easy routing. Next, consider data: a relational store like MySQL handles inventory, orders, and users with strong consistency. Finally, the front end: Bootstrap supplies responsive components so you can turn your mock‑ups into real pages fast. Together these three cover the three tiers we just discussed, match common skill sets, and scale as the store grows. Now let's see a tiny Flask starter file. It creates an app, defines a route, and runs on localhost. Remember: pick tools that fit your people, your performance needs, and your timeline. As a next step, write a one‑page README that lists Flask, MySQL, and Bootstrap as your chosen stack.
